evidence: tests/unit/test_cli_review_alias.py:273-275 `for mod in (review_workflows, eval_solver, mcp_llm): src = Path(mod.__file__).read_text(encoding="utf-8"); assert "_review_ticket_impl" in src`
Docstring falsely claims behavioral basis: tests/unit/test_cli_review_alias.py:266 `Asserted on the resolved call target, not on source text` — but the body reads source text

review_workflows.py:86 and eval_solver.py:310 route to `_review_ticket_impl` specifically so they emit no DeprecationWarning (ticket: 'Sites 4 and 5 ... must not warn'), yet only the MCP caller has a behavioral no-double-signal test (test_cli_review_alias.py:279 test_mcp_tool_emits_one_signal)

ABSENCE: `search_files` for `DeprecationWarning` across tests shows no test recording/asserting warning-free behavior for review_workflows.diff_review_paths or eval_solver — the single-signal contract for these two callers is guarded only by the substring grep
advisory.finding: `test_internal_callers_use_the_silent_impl` asserts by grepping the SOURCE TEXT of the units under test (`assert "_review_ticket_impl" in src` over each module's `__file__`), which is a source-grepping change-detector: it tests implementation text rather than observable behavior, passes even if the string appears only in a comment, and breaks on a behavior-preserving refactor (e.g. aliasing the import). It is also the ONLY guard that the `review_workflows` and `eval_solver` callers do not emit the deprecation warning — those two internal callers have no behavioral single-signal test (only MCP does, via `test_mcp_tool_emits_one_signal`), so a regression where either caller reverts to the warning `review_ticket` wrapper would NOT be caught by any behavioral assertion.
scenarios: A refactor imports the impl under an alias (`from ...operations import _review_ticket_impl as _impl`) — the grep still passes but a real call-target regression could slip; conversely a comment mention would satisfy the grep with no real call.
A future edit reverts `review_workflows` or `eval_solver` to call the public `review_ticket` wrapper: eval output / diff-harness starts emitting DeprecationWarnings and no behavioral test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: For each internal caller, exercise it with a FakeRunner inside `warnings.catch_warnings(record=True)` and assert `[w for w in caught if issubclass(w.category, DeprecationWarning)] == []`, so the single-signal contract is verified on observed warning behavior rather than on the presence of a substring in the module source.
